intro: だけ draws a boundary: this much, and nothing past it. Usually the boundary is tight and だけ means "only, just" (水だけ, 少しだけ). After できる, 好きな or a verb of wanting or ability it is the far edge instead, "as much as": you go right up to the limit (できるだけ早く). Either way だけ itself is neutral; it states a limit and leaves the verb positive or negative as the sense requires.

skills.rule: Put だけ right after the word being limited to mean "only, just"; the verb keeps its normal polarity, positive or negative.
skills.explain:
だけ attaches to the exact word that is limited: 水だけ飲みました (I drank only water), 一人だけ来ました (only one person came), 少しだけ (just a little). It also follows verbs and adjectives: 見るだけです (I'm just looking), 名前を書くだけで登録できます (you can register just by writing your name).

だけ is a plain statement of the limit. Unlike しか it does not need a negative verb, and unlike ばかり it does not suggest "too much, again and again". If you add a negative verb, the negative applies to the limited item: 田中さんだけ来ませんでした means Mr Tanaka was the only one who did not come.

が and を are usually left out, or can come after だけ (水だけを飲む), but never before it: をだけ and がだけ are wrong. Other particles may come before or after: 田中さんにだけ話した and 田中さんだけに話した are both fine. "Not only X" is Xだけでなく / Xだけじゃなく.
patterns: [verb dictionary form] だけです  "just do X"
[noun] に / と / で + だけ
X だけでなく Y も  "not only X but also Y"

examples.jp: 水[みず]{だけ}飲[の]みました。
一人[ひとり]{だけ}来[き]ました。
少[すこ]し{だけ}待[ま]ってください。
見[み]る{だけ}でもいいですか。
examples.en: Is it all right if I just look?

examples.jp: この話[はなし]は田中[たなか]さんに{だけ}しました。
examples.en: I told only Mr Tanaka about this.

examples.jp: 名前[なまえ]を書[か]く{だけ}で登録[とうろく]できます。
examples.en: You can register just by writing your name.

contrast.note: しか means the same "only" but must take a negative verb and sounds like "no more than, not enough": 千円しかありません. だけ takes the verb as it is: 千円だけあります. Positive verb for "only": だけ. Negative verb for "only": しか.

ばかり means "nothing but, all the time", usually with disapproval: 肉ばかり食べる (he eats meat all the time). 肉だけ食べる states the limit neutrally (he eats only meat). A single individual or a one-off event cannot take ばかり: 一人だけ, never 一人ばかり for "only one".

mistakes.bad: 家[いえ]では日本語[にほんご]を{だけ}話[はな]します。
mistakes.good: 家[いえ]では日本語[にほんご]{だけ}話[はな]します。
mistakes.note: を cannot come before だけ. Drop it, or put it after: 日本語だけを話します.

mistakes.bad: 今朝[けさ]は水[みず]{だけ}飲[の]みませんでした。
mistakes.good: 今朝[けさ]は水[みず]{だけ}飲[の]みました。
mistakes.note: For "I only drank water" the verb stays positive. だけ + negative means water was the one thing you did not drink. With a negative verb you need しか: 水しか飲みませんでした.

skills.tip: English "only" and the Japanese verb is positive: だけ. If the verb is negative and you still mean "only", it is しか.

skills.rule: できる / 好きな / a potential or たい verb + だけ means "as much as possible, as much as you like": go all the way to the limit.
skills.explain:
Here だけ marks the far edge of a range, not a small amount. The fixed phrase できるだけ means "as ... as possible": できるだけ早く来てください. 好きなだけ and 欲しいだけ mean "as much as you like / want": 好きなだけ取ってください. A na-adjective needs な before だけ (好きなだけ), an i-adjective or verb connects directly.

With a verb, the first verb sets the limit and a second one usually repeats it: 食べたいだけ食べる (eat as much as you want), 持てるだけ持って帰る (carry home as much as you can), やれるだけやってみます (I'll do everything I can). The first verb is in the potential, たい or plain form.

The boundary is with ほど. ほど expresses a degree, "so much that" (泣くほど痛い, it hurts enough to make you cry); it never replaces できるだけ. In "the more ... the more" (XばXほど) ほど is the normal choice.
patterns: できるだけ [adverb / verb]  "as ... as possible"
好きなだけ / 欲しいだけ [verb]  "as much as you like"
[potential / たい verb] だけ [same verb]  "as much as one can / wants"

examples.jp: できる{だけ}早[はや]く来[き]てください。
examples.en: Please come as early as possible.

examples.jp: 好[す]きな{だけ}取[と]ってください。
examples.en: Take as much as you like.

examples.jp: 食[た]べたい{だけ}食[た]べていいですよ。
examples.en: You can eat as much as you want.

examples.jp: 持[も]てる{だけ}持[も]って帰[かえ]りました。
examples.en: I took home as much as I could carry.

examples.jp: 結果[けっか]はともかく、やれる{だけ}やってみます。
examples.en: Whatever the result, I'll do all I can.

contrast.note: ほど gives a degree, "to the point that": 死ぬほど疲れた (tired enough to die). だけ gives the full amount available or wanted: 寝たいだけ寝た (I slept as much as I wanted). For "as ... as possible" only できるだけ works.
しか shrinks the amount to "no more than" and needs a negative verb. できるだけ / 好きなだけ stretch it to the maximum and take a positive verb.

mistakes.bad: できる{ほど}早[はや]く来[き]てください。
mistakes.good: できる{だけ}早[はや]く来[き]てください。
mistakes.note: "As ... as possible" is always できるだけ.

mistakes.bad: 好[す]き{だけ}食[た]べてください。
mistakes.good: 好[す]きな{だけ}食[た]べてください。
mistakes.note: 好き is a na-adjective, so it needs な before だけ.

skills.tip: できる, 好きな, or a can / want verb before the blank, meaning "as much as": だけ.
